title: Align sharded rate-limit tallies for backfill reconciliation to prevent per-model double-counts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Symptoms: Console per-model token charts intermittently show 10-30% overcount after a backfill window runs (mostly for high-throughput tenants using Dedicated). The overcount appears as a sharp spike on the day of the backfill and persists in daily aggregates until a manual reconciliation job runs. Root cause hypothesis: our sharded rate-limiter service keeps in-memory timebucketed tallies per-shard and flushes periodic deltas to the canonical metrics stream. During backfill, ingestion writes historical events into the canonical store without marking that the in-memory shard deltas already reflected some of those events, so the same logical events are counted twice when the backfilled rows are ingested and the in-memory flush later emits overlapping deltas. This is most visible for per-model breakdowns because model attribution happens at ingest time and the reconciliation/aggregation pipeline treats the backfilled rows as additional usage rather than idempotent inserts.
acceptance_criteria: Console per-model daily token totals must not increase more than 0.5% after applying a backfill for affected time ranges
Backfill ingestion is idempotent: running the same backfill job twice must not change canonical aggregates
Dashboard shows a new "adjusted_backfill" flag for any series where historical rows were rewritten
Reconciliation job completes within SLA (see Implementation Notes) and clears historical mismatch alerts
implementation_notes: Add last_ingest_offset and backfill_marker metadata per-rate-limiter-shard in Cassandra so flushes are aware of which historical time ranges were later backfilled
When backfill ingestion writes historical rows, include an 'event_uuid' and 'is_backfill' boolean; ingestion pipeline must perform upsert semantics keyed by event_uuid to avoid duplicates
Modify shard flush process to consult last_ingest_offset and skip emitting deltas for backfilled windows already materialized in canonical store
Update aggregation materialized view to prefer canonical store counts when is_backfill=true OR event_uuid exists
Small DB migration: add columns (event_uuid uuid, is_backfill boolean, backfill_tag varchar) to the usage_events table; run in two phases with feature flag backfill_v2
Introduce a lightweight reconciliation runner that deduplicates rows by event_uuid for the last 90 days; schedule as low-priority batch to run during off-peak to avoid load spikes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (client-visible opt-in): Deploy ingestion changes behind feature flag 'backfill_v2' and enable for internal tenants only
Phase 2 (shard metadata): Deploy last_ingest_offset to shards; run a migration that backfills last_ingest_offset from the canonical store for each shard
Phase 3 (idempotent ingest): Flip 'backfill_v2' to true for all ingestion traffic; monitor reconciliation metrics
Phase 4 (reconcile): Run dedupe job for past 90 days; only mark charts as 'adjusted' after automated tests verify totals
Phase 5 (cleanup): Remove feature flag and deprecated paths after 30 days of stable metrics
qa_steps: Create test tenancy that uses multiple rate-limiter shards and generate synthetic events that intentionally overlap with a simulated backfill
Run backfill_v2 in opt-in mode and validate that the canonical aggregates are unchanged when backfill is re-run
Assert that console per-model charts expose 'adjusted_backfill' annotation and tooltips explain the adjustment
Load test reconciliation runner on staging dataset ~2x production peak to ensure CPU and DB IO remain below thresholds
Create alert to detect >1% discrepancy between canonical aggregates and per-shard flushes for a 24h window during rollout
estimated_risks: Schema migration could increase write amplification temporarily; mitigation: conservative batch migration with throttling
Dedupe job could cause increased DB IO and impact other analytics workloads; mitigation: run at low priority and throttle
Incorrect event_uuid generation for old events could lead to incomplete dedupe; mitigation: keep legacy dedupe fallback using hash of (timestamp, user_id, request_id)
Charts that apply smoothing may still visually misrepresent short-lived corrections; mitigation: annotate adjusted windows and provide raw toggle

2026-03-11 - Darren O'Neill: Reproduced locally by running a sharded flush simulator + backfill. Confirmed overlap in timebucket boundaries where in-memory shard flush emits deltas for the same logical events later inserted by backfill.
